# Logistics 0.2.0 alpha 2

This alpha updates mobile Documents and Notes Library navigation, filename search, embedded source-file editing, Markdown links and Data View rendering. Accent text and controls use the same selected color in light and dark appearance. Android hue/saturation controls have larger thumbs and touch areas; dragging updates the preview and release applies the color across the app. File moves show copy/encryption and verification progress; cancellation and privacy locking preserve safe cleanup. Encrypted comic reads avoid repeated decryption, and fullscreen playback avoids an idle layout loop. Notes Library search defaults to filenames and preserves separate Files/Search lists. Individual library notes appear in Recent and reopen in their library. Documents has a dedicated filename-search action, compact file/folder result rows and an exit control; Android Back returns to the previous collection. Standalone Markdown previews omit the file-drawer menu. Please test library navigation, unsaved changes, local and encrypted documents, data views, video playback and compact layouts. Report the platform, build number, reproduction steps and observed result.

Please verify that marked Notes Libraries in Local and unlocked LocalCrypt appear automatically in Documents, including libraries accessed with Session-Only credentials. Open a detected library, navigate nested notes, use Back/Forward and lock credentials. Also pull an updated file while it is open as a document: the transfer should complete, any unsaved draft should remain available, and a stale save should not overwrite the pulled content.

Notes Library Data Views: users may author or import Markdown notes containing complete, top-level `dataviewjs` blocks and JavaScript view files in their own selected library. These user-supplied scripts execute automatically when the containing note is opened in Notes Library reading mode on desktop or mobile; there is currently no separate library-trust prompt. Opening a JavaScript source file in the editor does not execute it. JSON files are data: a user-authored script may read and parse them to produce tables, lists, links and other supported document views. JSON itself is not executable code.

The implementation is an independent, limited Data View compatibility layer, not an Obsidian plugin host. Scripts execute in a disposable browser worker with a 30-second execution limit. Supported native requests provide bounded reads and Markdown metadata inside the selected library; paths outside the library and hidden configuration are rejected. Scripts do not receive the native application API or the document DOM. The worker document's content security policy restricts network access, and rendered output is escaped or constructed through the supported display helpers. Script and output limits apply. Source blocks remain editable in the user's note; generated results are display content. Users should inspect code in notes and view files they import before opening those notes in reading mode.

This alpha includes fixes for iPad Workspaces sidebar cleanup and redundant navigation-bar changes during rotation. Intermittent native crashes and WebKit page-loading stalls have been observed in automated iOS simulator testing; investigation continues. Please report any navigation, loading or rotation failure with the device, OS, build number and reproduction steps.
